title: AshML — Models & deployments
description: The spec's §49 asks a dashboard to show models — their versions and status — and deployments. Prometheus can count those (`ashml_model_versions`, `ashml_deployments`) and a count is not the question anyone actually has, which is *which* version is in production and whether the bytes behind it were ever confirmed. So the two tables here come from PostgreSQL, the same second datasource the training curves use (ADR 0010), and the counts above them come from Prometheus.

panels.title: Versions in PRODUCTION
panels.description: At most one per model, enforced in the same transaction that promotes (Phase 4).

panels.title: Versions in STAGING
panels.description: Where a displaced production version goes — the most likely rollback target, so it is not archived by the promotion that replaced it.

panels.title: Deployments READY
panels.description: Observed from the cluster's readyReplicas, never assumed from having created the objects.

panels.title: Deployments DEGRADED
panels.description: Was serving and is now short of replicas. Kept distinct from PROGRESSING, because one word for both hides an outage inside something that sounds like startup.

panels.title: Registered versions
panels.description: `bytes_confirmed` is the column worth reading. A version can only be registered from a READY artifact, and READY means AshML asked the store whether the bytes arrived — `NO` means they are stored somewhere it cannot check, not that they are missing. A registry entry pointing at unconfirmed bytes moves the discovery from "the upload failed" to "production cannot load the model".

targets.rawSql:
SELECT p.name                                   AS project,
       m.name                                   AS model,
       v.version                                AS version,
       v.status                                 AS status,
       coalesce(a.status, 'none')               AS artifact,
       CASE
         WHEN a.id IS NULL                          THEN 'no artifact'
         WHEN (a.metadata->>'verified')::boolean    THEN 'yes'
         WHEN a.metadata ? 'verified'               THEN 'NO'
         ELSE 'unchecked'
       END                                      AS bytes_confirmed,
       left(coalesce(a.id::text, ''), 8)        AS artifact_id,
       v.created_at                             AS registered,
       v.promoted_at                            AS promoted
  FROM model_versions v
  JOIN models   m ON m.id = v.model_id
  JOIN projects p ON p.id = m.project_id
  LEFT JOIN artifacts a ON a.id = v.artifact_id
 ORDER BY p.name, m.name, v.version DESC

panels.title: Deployments
panels.description: `address_resolves_to` is what the front Service currently selects, which is not always what `split` asks for: the address only moves onto a version once that version has a ready pod, so during a rollout these two disagree and that disagreement is the switch in progress. Empty means the address is on the router, which is where it goes when more than one version takes traffic.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT p.name                                    AS project,
       d.name                                    AS deployment,
       m.name                                    AS model,
       d.status                                  AS status,
       d.serving_version                         AS address_resolves_to,
       d.ready_replicas || '/' || d.replicas     AS replicas,
       coalesce(string_agg('v' || v.version || ' ' || t.traffic_weight || '%',
                           '  ' ORDER BY v.version), '-')  AS split,
       coalesce(d.router_status, '-')            AS router,
       coalesce(d.last_error, '')                AS last_error,
       d.endpoint_url                            AS endpoint
  FROM deployments d
  JOIN projects p ON p.id = d.project_id
  JOIN models   m ON m.id = d.model_id
  LEFT JOIN deployment_targets t ON t.deployment_id = d.id
  LEFT JOIN model_versions     v ON v.id = t.model_version_id
 GROUP BY p.name, d.name, m.name, d.status, d.serving_version,
          d.ready_replicas, d.replicas, d.router_status, d.last_error, d.endpoint_url
 ORDER BY p.name, d.name
